question:
Patient note:
A 55-year-old woman is reviewed this morning in the orthopaedic ward ahead of a scheduled left total knee replacement that the surgical team estimates will require roughly two hours of tourniquet time under general anaesthesia with planned cemented components and immediate postoperative weight-bearing as tolerated. Four days ago she was admitted for pre-operative optimisation after reporting progressively disabling mechanical knee pain that prevented her from completing household chores; since arrival she has remained largely supine with nursing documentation noting only assisted transfers to a bedside commode, and physical therapy has deferred ambulation until after the operation because of intolerable joint crepitus on even minimal range-of-motion exercises. She states that the upcoming procedure will be her first time in an operating theatre since an uncomplicated abdominal hysterectomy performed more than five years ago; she has not undergone any endoscopic, vascular, or interventional radiology procedure in the past several months. Past medical history is notable for a stage II oestrogen-receptor–positive breast carcinoma diagnosed eight years earlier that was treated with left modified radical mastectomy, adjuvant doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide followed by tamoxifen for five years, and interval imaging and mammography have shown no evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease—she takes no ongoing anti-neoplastic therapy and her most recent oncology visit six weeks ago documented stable labs and a clear chest radiograph. She denies prior episodes of calf tenderness, unilateral leg swelling, or chest pain suggestive of thrombo-embolic disease, and duplex ultrasonography obtained during last year’s varicose-vein work-up demonstrated fully compressible deep venous segments bilaterally. She has never needed oral anticoagulation, her first-degree relatives have no history of unexplained clotting, and she has not been tested for inherited coagulation abnormalities. Chronic conditions include well-controlled hypertension managed with amlodipine 5 mg daily and diet-controlled hyperlipidaemia; she specifically denies heart-failure admissions, chronic lung disease, bowel-inflammatory symptoms, connective-tissue disorders, or recent fevers, rigors, or sputum-producing cough. She quit smoking twenty years ago after a 10-pack-year exposure, enjoys a single glass of wine on weekends, and does not use hormonal replacement, glucocorticoids, selective oestrogen-receptor modulators, or erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. She has not worn casts or braces, sustained fractures, or experienced high-energy trauma in the past year. This morning she appears alert, oriented, and converses easily from the high-low hospital bed with the head elevated thirty degrees. Vital signs recorded fifteen minutes earlier show temperature 36.7 °C, blood pressure 132/78 mm Hg, heart rate 76 beats min⁻¹ in regular rhythm, respiratory rate 14 min⁻¹, and oxygen saturation 98 % on room air; body-mass index is 29 kg m⁻². Airway assessment reveals Mallampati class II, intact dentition, and full cervical extension. Jugular venous pressure lies beneath the clavicular heads, carotid upstrokes are brisk, S₁ and S₂ are crisp without murmurs, gallops, or rubs, and lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. The abdomen is soft and non-tender with a well-healed transverse suprapubic scar. Inspection of both lower limbs discloses serpiginous, bluish superficial veins coursing along the medial calves and posterior thighs; the overlying skin is warm and dry, there is no pitting oedema, calf circumferences measured 10 cm below the tibial tuberosities are symmetric at 36 cm, and no palpable cords or tenderness are elicited. Knee examination shows crepitus through flexion-extension arc with varus deformity and fixed flexion contracture of 10 degrees on the left, whereas neurovascular status of the feet is intact with posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis pulses 2+. Neurologic screen reveals 5/5 strength in the unaffected extremities, intact sensation to light touch, and brisk deep-tendon reflexes. Skin over both upper limbs shows only a single 20-gauge peripheral IV cannula in the right cephalic vein running lactated Ringer’s at keep-open rate; no tunneled catheters, implanted ports, or peripherally inserted central lines are present. Morning laboratory studies drawn at 05:00 report haemoglobin 13.4 g dL⁻¹, haematocrit 40 %, platelets 245 × 10⁹ L⁻¹, leukocytes 6.9 × 10⁹ L⁻¹, sodium 139 mmol L⁻¹, potassium 4.0 mmol L⁻¹, bicarbonate 24 mmol L⁻¹, creatinine 0.89 mg dL⁻¹, AST 22 U L⁻¹, ALT 24 U L⁻¹, total bilirubin 0.6 mg dL⁻¹, prothrombin time 12.1 s with international normalised ratio 1.0, and activated partial thromboplastin time 29 s. A twelve-lead electrocardiogram reviewed by anaesthesia shows normal sinus rhythm at 74 beats min⁻¹ with normal intervals and no ST-T wave abnormalities compared with a tracing from her primary-care visit three months prior. Pre-operative chest radiograph obtained on admission depicts clear lungs and unremarkable cardiomediastinal silhouette. Sequential compression sleeves are wrapped around both calves but remain deflated pending draping, no chemoprophylactic anticoagulant has been administered thus far, and she has been nil per os since midnight after taking her usual antihypertensive with a sip of water.

Question: What is the patient's Caprini Score for Venous Thromboembolism?
solution:
The Caprini VTE score sums applicable perioperative risk factors:
- Age 55 (41–60 years) → 1.
- BMI 29 kg/m² (>25) → 1.
- Visible varicose veins → 1.
- Bed confinement for >72 hours: four days largely supine with only assisted commode transfers → 2.
- Current or prior malignancy: treated breast cancer counts despite remission → 2.
- Planned elective lower-extremity arthroplasty: total knee replacement → 5. Do not also score the same operation as generic major surgery lasting >45 minutes.
No additional points are supported for prior VTE, family history of thrombosis, known thrombophilia, hormone use, or central venous access; the IV is peripheral.
Total = 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 5 = 12.
Final answer: 12
